planting.note: Set out container plants in spring in sharply drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Kahori was a widely grown American Garden Award entrant valued for its hardy-carnation-type flowers on a compact mound.

directions: Kahori bears semi-double, bright pink-lilac, clove-scented flowers in continuous flushes from late spring through summer and into early fall above a tidy mound of silvery-blue, evergreen foliage. It stays compact and self-cleaning, needing only light deadheading to keep the bloom cycle going, and the fine foliage provides color even when the plant is not in flower. Grow in full sun with sharply drained soil; once established it tolerates short dry spells and resents soggy winter conditions far more than drought.

common_name: Bright Light Dianthus (Vivid Carmine-Red Hardy Carnation)

planting.note: Set out container plants in spring in sharply drained, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in full sun; Bright Light was bred in Korea from Dianthus alpinus and D. callizonus as an improvement on the older hardy-carnation standard 'Kahori'.

directions: Bright Light opens dense, sweetly fragrant, carmine-red flowers beginning in mid-spring above a tight, silver-foliaged clump, with notably better heat and heavy-rainfall tolerance in southern gardens than older hardy carnations. The low, spreading habit holds its silvery evergreen leaves as a neat groundcover year-round. Grow in full sun with excellent drainage, and avoid heavy, wet soils that encourage crown rot. Light shearing after the main spring flush can tidy the mound and may encourage secondary bloom.

common_name: EverLast Burgundy Blush Dianthus (Reblooming Burgundy-Red Pink with Frosted Edges)

planting.note: Set out container plants in spring in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Burgundy Blush is part of the EverLast dianthus series bred for an extended three-season bloom cycle.

directions: Burgundy Blush carries double, spicy clove-scented flowers in deep burgundy-red with a frosted picotee edge of soft pink, held above a compact mound of blue-green evergreen foliage. Like other EverLast series pinks it flushes heavily in spring, continues into summer, and rebounds with a strong fall flush as nights cool, drawing butterflies and hummingbirds throughout. Grow in full sun with sharply drained soil and even moisture; deadhead spent stems to keep flushes coming. It performs well in mixed containers, border edges, and mass bedding.

common_name: EverLast Peach Dianthus (Reblooming Soft Peach-Pink Garden Pink)

planting.note: Set out container plants in spring in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Peach is part of the EverLast dianthus series bred for an extended three-season bloom cycle.

directions: EverLast Peach bears clove-scented, soft peach-pink flowers with subtle tonal shading over a compact, blue-green mound, opening in heavy flushes from spring through summer with a second strong show as temperatures cool in fall. Regular deadheading extends each flush and keeps the mounded habit tidy through the growing season. Give it full sun and sharply drained soil, since like other garden pinks it is intolerant of wet feet, especially over winter. It suits border edges, rock gardens, and mixed containers.

common_name: EverLast White Eye Dianthus (Reblooming White with Violet-Red Eye)

planting.note: Set out container plants in spring in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; White Eye is part of the EverLast dianthus series bred for an extended three-season bloom cycle.

directions: EverLast White Eye opens frilly, fragrant double flowers in crisp white centered with a violet-red eye, carried over a compact mound of fine gray-green, evergreen foliage. Bloom is heaviest in late spring, continues through summer, and rebounds in a distinct fall flush, with the strongly bicolor blooms also holding up well as cut flowers. Grow in full sun with sharply drained soil and even moisture, deadheading to prolong each flowering cycle. It works well massed as edging or combined in containers with other sun-loving perennials.
